subject: Telemetry add-ons: price framing and bundle examples
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina@datacraft.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@datacraft.ai>
Date: 2027-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry add-ons: price framing and bundle examples

Hi Nina / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited by the telemetry use case you outlined (heavy trace ingestion from sampler pipelines + 30M embedding calls/month). You mentioned wanting clarity on how observability add-ons map to costs (retention tiers, tracing volume, advanced dashboards). I pulled together a short framing and a couple of illustrative bundle examples to make procurement conversations smoother.

Quick ask: can you confirm your current monthly telemetry volumes (spans ingested, average span length, index/trace retention window) and whether the dashboards will be for internal ops only or also customer-facing? If you can attach your current usage export I can tailor numbers.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I’ll send 2–3 priced bundle scenarios (low/medium/high) with first-year credit paths and sample SOW language.
- If you’re comfortable, we’ll propose a commercial concession for year one to offset migration costs and show quick ROI.

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Telemetry add-ons: price framing and bundle examples

Hi Karthik,

Thanks — attaching a short export of our telemetry usage for July-Aug (sanitized): spans_ingested.csv and a short product note on which dashboards are customer-facing. Key bits:
- Avg spans/day: 12M (peak 18M)
- Typical trace depth: 8–20 events
- Expect 2x growth in 6 months as we onboard two new customers
- We need a 90-day retention for customer-facing dashboards and 365-day for internal troubleshooting.

We’re sensitive to tokenized pricing for tracing and the incremental charge for longer retention. Procurement wants concrete bundle examples and a clear explanation of any credits for year-one onboarding.

Attachment: usage_summary.csv (CSV, 34KB)

—Nina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina@datacraft.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@datacraft.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-22T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry add-ons: price framing and bundle examples

Thanks for the export, Nina — that helps a lot. I chatted with our product ops and finance teams and sketched three bundle examples and the logic behind retention pricing. High level: retention and tracing are orthogonal to text-generation token pricing; we price traces by ingested spans + retention tier, and dashboards are an add-on seat + visualization SKU for customer-facing rollout.

Attached: draft_sku_pricing.xlsx (workbook with three scenarios). Summary below (rounded):

Scenario A — Starter (for pilot)
- 90-day retention (ops + limited customer dashboards)
- Trace ingestion: up to 15M spans/month
- Dashboards: 10 customer-facing visualizations included
- List price: $6,500/month
- Year-one concession: 25% credit applied to observability add-ons (not core inference) if committed 12 months

Scenario B — Production (expected fit)
- 365-day internal retention, 90-day customer-facing retention
- Trace ingestion: up to 40M spans/month
- Dashboards: 50 visualizations + role-based access
- List price: $21,000/month
- Year-one concession: $30k onboarding credit (applied as stipend against first 3 invoices)

Scenario C — Enterprise (high volume, long retention)
- 365-day retention full scope
- Trace ingestion: up to 120M spans/month
- Dashboards: unlimited visualizations, dedicated reporting node
- List price: $62,000/month
- Year-one concession: custom credits + 6-month pricing step-down on retention storage

Notes & clarifications:
- Retention storage is metered monthly and priced per GB-month; longer retention can be partially offset by tiered compression and archive pathways.
- Dashboards charge includes rendering & export for customer-facing views; internal ops dashboards billed as part of retention tier.
- Concessions are conditional on contract length (12–36 months) and minimum committed billing.

Can you confirm which scenario is closest to your expectation? I’m looping Laura for commercial approval on the concession language and Vivek on technical feasibility of the dedicated reporting node mentioned in Scenario C.

Attachment: draft_sku_pricing.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-23T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry add-ons: price framing and bundle examples

Karthik — quick internal: I reviewed the scenarios. We can greenlight a commercial concession along these lines for DataCraft given their ARR profile and clean procurement path:

Approved concession framework (internal):
- Up to 20% off observability add-on list pricing in year one (or $30k onboarding credit, whichever is greater).
- Concession valid for 12–24 month committed terms; for >24 months we can extend to 25% on a case-by-case basis.
- No concession on the core inference token pricing; concessions apply only to telemetry add-ons (retention, tracing, dashboards).
- Require a single SOW that outlines migration milestones and acceptance tests for dashboards.

Please include this language in the external proposal. Also Vivek — confirm that a dedicated reporting node for Scenario C is feasible without >8-week lead time; if not, flag as custom engineering and we’ll price separately.

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0111
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-24T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: telemetry add-on bundles + year-one concession (DataCraft)

Nina / Tom —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on usage. Based on your volumes and growth plans we think Scenario B (Production) maps best, and below is the concise commercial proposal you can share with procurement.

External proposal (concise)
- Recommended: Scenario B — Production bundle (365-day internal retention, 90-day customer-facing retention; up to 40M spans/month; 50 visualizations)
- List price: $21,000/month for telemetry add-ons (retention + tracing + dashboards)
- Year-one concession: $30,000 onboarding credit applied across first three invoices OR 20% off telemetry add-ons in year one (your choice).
- Contract term: 12 months minimum; we offer stepped pricing for 24–36 month commitments.
- Deliverables: migration plan, SOW, acceptance tests for dashboards, and knowledge transfer sessions.

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want Scenario B + which concession option you prefer.
2) We’ll issue a redlined commercial SOW and Fence Doc; procurement can then issue PO.
3) Kickoff within two weeks of signed SOW (assuming onboarding credit accepted).

Attachments included with this mail: SOW_Template.docx (DOCX, 62KB) and the earlier usage export. Also here’s a HubSpot link to the deal record and the draft SKU workbook for reference: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/DC-2027-091 and https://drive.redwood/shared/telemetry-bundle-examples

If procurement prefers the $30k onboarding credit, we’ll reflect that in the SOW billing schedule. Happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the credit mechanics.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
